---
name: token-optimizer-share
description: >-
  Use when wiring or reviewing the shareable token-optimizer package (gateway
  plan/send, check-api-key, safe defaults, scoped honesty).
---
# token-optimizer (share edition 0.2.21)

Portable wiring. No private agent IDs. No hardcoded host paths.

## Ship artifact
- Package: the token-optimizer share zip, version 0.2.21
- Verdict: scoped, not "zero caveats"; in-app chats are not covered (no platform hook)

## Environment
```bash
export TOKEN_OPTIMIZER_ROOT="/absolute/path/to/token-optimizer"
export PATH="$TOKEN_OPTIMIZER_ROOT/bin:$PATH"
# Optional kill switch: TOKEN_OPT_GATEWAY_DISABLED=1
```
The root variable is a convenience for these commands; the `bin/` scripts also resolve the package root from their own location. Use whatever root variable your package's README names.

## Automatic work (only when policy allows)
When `gateway/policy.json` has `enabled: true` and your namespace is allowlisted, `bin/gateway plan|send` or `gateway.client.send` applies only the policy's `auto_apply` stages. Shipped share policy (`enabled: false` until you allowlist):
- On: `dedupe_tools`, `coalesce_exact_messages` (exact copies only), `stabilize_cache` (canonical JSON key order in tool definitions/arguments), `sort_tools` (tool definitions in name order), `anthropic_auto_cache` (Anthropic-shaped bodies only, `provider_format="anthropic"`, plan-only; refused when the system prompt has a timestamp/request-id line).
- Off: `json_minify_tool_results`, `near_dup_append` (experimental), every lossy layer. Old-turn summarization and timestamp relocation are not in the package.
- Bare `Options()` is identity. Apply caching settings from turn 1 of a conversation.

## Measured (cite with model and date; list-price run costs, not savings)
- Repeat x3, 2026-10-11, key-order-unstable client vs raw: gpt-4o-mini -20.9%, grok-4.20-0309-non-reasoning -49.9%, claude-haiku-4-5 -55.3% (docs/CACHE_PLANNING.md).
- `sort_tools` (on): tool selection unchanged live, 0/162 ON-only (Wilson 95% upper 2.3%), tool_choice auto, 3 providers; on a client that reorders tools, run cost -26.6% / -50.7% / -72.7% vs unsorted (without it Anthropic cost +24.8% vs no caching).
- JSON minify: single-turn 0/85 ON-only answer failures, multi-turn 3/75 (Wilson 95% upper 11.1%), so it stays off.

## Must not claim
- Native Grok Bot / Cursor harness turns are optimized (they are UNCOVERED)
- Dollar savings, or compression and caching savings added together
- Lossy layers, minify or summarization as safe defaults
- "Zero caveats" or a full quality suite from a bounded live smoke alone

## Commands
```bash
python3 -m optimizer_bot demo
"$TOKEN_OPTIMIZER_ROOT/bin/gateway" plan examples/request.json \
  --namespace YOUR_NAMESPACE --context-version YOUR_CONTEXT_VERSION
"$TOKEN_OPTIMIZER_ROOT/bin/check-api-key"   # metadata only; never prints the secret
"$TOKEN_OPTIMIZER_ROOT/bin/gateway" status
```
Before live send: `OPTIMIZER_API_KEY`, or `OPTIMIZER_API_KEY_FILE` pointing at a one-line key file.

## Tenancy
1. Allowlist only namespaces you control
2. Keep `enabled: false` until that list is correct
3. Distinct namespaces per account/project
4. Protect runtime `.optimizer/` (not shipped in the zip)

## Coverage
COVERED = deliberate gateway / optimize calls you invoke. UNCOVERED = native harness and any path that never imports this package.

---
name: optimizer-getting-started
description: >-
  Use when a newly imported token-optimizer bot runs its first conversation with
  a new owner and needs setup answers.
---
I cut the token cost of your LLM requests and prompts without losing meaning: exact duplicates removed, cache-friendly prefixes, every rule kept. Lossy steps only with your OK.

Ask, one at a time:
1. Do you have the token-optimizer package? If yes, its path. If no, I work by hand on pasted text.
2. Which provider and model do your requests go to (OpenAI, xAI, Anthropic, other)?
3. Which namespace should I use for your gateway calls?

Then: save the answers as memories, run `bin/gateway status` offline, and offer one offline `plan` on a sample request. Mention that the shipped policy starts disabled with an empty allowlist, and that tool sorting and cache-key stabilization are on once they enable it.
Never ask for API keys in chat; live runs only with your OK.
